could_not_do: THE BIGGEST ONE, found by doing exactly what the owner's directive asks (look at real production content, not just the test fixture): on REAL settlement ground (Thorn, VP04's surveyed pose) the SSAO reads every low-poly terrain TRIANGLE's own flat facet as a separate plane, because the surface normal is reconstructed from a one-pixel screen-space depth derivative rather than a smooth interpolated vertex normal — there is no G-buffer normal target in this pipeline to read instead. At the tuning that passes the RI-VIS04 bar cleanly (radius 0.42, strength 1.9), this reads on real ground as a hard black-diamond checker matching the terrain's own triangulation, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. Mitigated, not solved: radius down to 0.16 m (samples stay closer to one facet), and a hard cap on total occlusion (uAOMaxOcclusion, currently 0.32) so the worst case is a visible grey crease rather than solid black. This softens it considerably but does NOT remove it — it is still visible as a faint geometric grid on open ground in the evidence screenshots. The real fix is a smooth/interpolated normal (a G-buffer target, or reading a vertex-normal attribute already on the terrain mesh) and is out of scope for a compositor-only change; named as owed below.

W1-ORPHANED-SURFACE-SHADERS (V1, landed same day) found and recorded the actual AO gap directly: worldMaterial() sets aoMap:null on every family with an authored set (all twenty), and 'there is no screen-space AO pass anywhere in game/src/render — only a comment in visual-foundation.js:676 deferring to W1-30A's GTAO stack, which does not exist in the tree.' MATERIAL_API.md is frozen (§9: additions only). This fix does not touch worldMaterial(), the twenty families, or any option key — it is entirely inside the compositor, which is not part of the frozen surface.

the_fix.mechanism: Ten-tap hemisphere SSAO. viewPosFromDepth() reconstructs view-space position from the existing depth texture and the camera's projectionMatrixInverse (pushed every frame from renderer.js — the camera moves every frame). Normal is estimated from the position's own screen-space derivative (cross(dFdx(P),dFdy(P))), the standard technique when no G-buffer normal exists. Ten hardcoded, hemisphere-biased kernel samples (deterministic — no per-frame randomness, matching the existing dither pass's own determinism requirement) are rotated per-pixel by the same static interleaved-gradient-noise hash the dither already uses, offset from P, re-projected to screen space via the camera's forward projectionMatrix, and compared against the real depth there with a distance range check. uAO stays the on/off name and meaning every existing tool (tools/render/w1-30-*.mjs) already flips; what changed is what it does when on.
the_fix.new_uniforms: uProjMat, uInvProjMat (mat4, pushed every frame), uAORadius (0.42 m default), uAOStrength (1.4), uAOBias (0.018 m) — all additive to the existing uniform set, nothing removed or renamed.
the_fix.why_no_shader_hook_collision: This is a self-contained THREE.ShaderMaterial fragment shader already owned by render/post/composite.js since W1-30S/A. It does not touch THREE.ShaderChunk at module scope (the two known collision sites are game/src/world/aerial.js and game/src/render/sky.js, both fog). tools/visual/w1-30-shader-hook-collision.mjs run before and after this change (see gates_run) to prove that.

the_bug_found_and_fixed_while_building_t: The first working version of computeAO() sent the estimated view-space normal the WRONG way (`if (N.z > 0.0) N = -N`), which points every hemisphere kernel sample INTO the surface instead of out over it. Measured effect: the ENTIRE FRAME went solid black end to end whenever uAO was on (screenshot evidence in the scratchpad probe history; not carried into the evidence pack since it is a dev-time defect, not a shipped one). Confirmed and fixed by working out the view-space sign convention on paper (camera looks down -Z, a front-facing normal has positive Z) and flipping the condition to `if (N.z < 0.0) N = -N`. Recorded here because RULES rule 4 asks that a probe capable of failing be shown failing, and this is that evidence for the shader itself, not just for the gate around it — and because a wrong-signed normal is exactly the kind of error a screenshot catches and a stats-only check would not, which is why boot-check (engine constructs) passed the whole time this was broken: it never renders and inspects a frame.
